english: Let $C$ be the locus of the complex numbers $z$ satisfying $|z|=3|z-4|$. The ray $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ meets $C$ at two points $P$ and $Q$. If $O$ is the origin, then the value of $OP\cdot OQ$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ उन सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का बिन्दुपथ है जो $|z|=3|z-4|$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं। किरण $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{12}$, $C$ को दो बिन्दुओं $P$ तथा $Q$ पर मिलती है। यदि $O$ मूल बिन्दु है, तो $OP\cdot OQ$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $C$: $x^{2}+y^{2}=9\left((x-4)^{2}+y^{2}\right)\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-9x+18=0$, circle with centre $\dfrac{9}{2}$, radius $\dfrac{3}{2}$; $O$ is outside
Discriminant $81\cos^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{12}-72>0$ ($\cos^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{12}\approx0.933$) and both roots are positive, so the ray meets $C$ twice
$OP\cdot OQ=r_{1}r_{2}=18$ (the power of $O$ with respect to $C$)
solution_full: So $C$ is the Apollonius circle $\left(x-\dfrac{9}{2}\right)^{2}+y^{2}=\dfrac{9}{4}$: centre $\dfrac{9}{2}$, radius $\dfrac{3}{2}$. (It meets the real axis at $3$ and $6$, which divide the segment from $0$ to $4$ internally and externally in the ratio $3:1$.)
Points of the ray $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ are $z=r\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{12}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$ with $r>0$, and $x^{2}+y^{2}=r^{2}$, $x=r\cos\dfrac{\pi}{12}$.

The discriminant is $81\cos^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{12}-72=81\cdot\dfrac{2+\sqrt{3}}{4}-72>0$; the sum $9\cos\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ and the product $18$ of the roots are positive, so both roots are positive and give the points $P,Q$ on the ray. (Also $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}<\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{3/2}{9/2}$, so the ray cuts the circle.)
Hence $OP\cdot OQ=r_{1}r_{2}=18$, which is the power of $O$: $0^{2}+0^{2}-9\cdot0+18=18$.
originality_note: New: the product of the two intercepts of a ray from one Apollonius point on the Apollonius circle is the power of that point, k^2|AB|^2/(k^2-1), independent of the ray (way 4, invariant). Closest known: the Apollonius circle |z - a| = k|z - b| and its centre and radius. Different because: the ray, not the circle, is the object asked about, and the answer comes from Vieta (power of a point) rather than from the intersection points.
blueprint_concepts: Circle in complex form; Apollonius locus |z-z1|/|z-z2| = k
Perpendicular bisector, ray and angle loci

concept_use.Circle in complex form; Apollonius locus: |z| = 3|z-4| is converted to the circle x^2+y^2-9x+18 = 0 (centre 9/2, radius 3/2).
concept_use.Perpendicular bisector, ray and angle lo: arg z = pi/12 is the ray z = r e^{i pi/12}, r > 0; both roots must be positive to lie on the ray.

key_step: Substitute the ray z = r e^{i pi/12} into the Apollonius circle and use the product of roots r1 r2 = 18.
justification: Routine chain (Apollonius circle, parametrise the ray, Vieta) with a check that both points are on the ray; no insight. Level 2, above 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).
